business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Private Network and Digital Encryption Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law system with Anglo-Saxon corporate law influences in the regulation of Sociedades Anónimas)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force since 31 October 2012)
Panama-Republic of Korea Bilateral Investment Treaty
Panama-United Kingdom Double Taxation and Investment Convention
Panama-Canada Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework), as amended by Ley No. 58 de 2018 and Ley No. 115 de 2019; Ley No. 52 de 2016 (customer due diligence and reporting agent duties); Ley No. 70 de 2019 establishing the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales under Law 70 of 2019; Executive Decrees No. 201 and No. 202 de 2016; UAF Resolution No. 001 of 2020 (PEP and sanctions screening). The mandatory UBO register is implemented by Ministry of Economy and Finance Resolution No. 445 of 2021 and related DGI instructions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the proposed shareholder's/UBO's passport (notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the passport's country of issue / Apostille Competent Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague member states, consular legalization at a Panama consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence or Good Standing (for corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Power of Attorney (Poder) appointing the Panamanian resident agent and/or subscriber
UBO/Settlor Declaration and AML questionnaire (Ficha del Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Law firm of origin; executed by each beneficial owner before a notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Panama Law 23/2015 and UAF Resolution No. 001 of 2020 mandate AML screening before incorporation. The licensed resident agent must verify shareholders and UBOs against the UAF domestic alert list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated sanctions list, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction alerts. Politically Exposed Persons require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, beneficial-ownership corroboration, and final compliance-officer approval. Adverse media and negative reputational data must also be assessed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Servicios en Línea, Module for Reserva de Razón Social (www.rpp.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All name reservations are processed in Latin script. If the proposed name uses a non-Latin alphabet, a phonetic transliteration in Latin letters must be provided. The statutory corporate type suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.' is mandatory. The Registry indexes names in Spanish; a Spanish translation or explanation of any foreign-language expression may be required by the Registry to avoid misleading or prohibited content.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a name reservation, the applicant or its attorney in fact may file a Recurso de Reconsideración before the Director General of the Registro Público within five business days of notification. If denied, a Recurso de Apelación may be submitted to the Junta Directiva of the Registro Público within five further business days. The appeal must quote the reservation receipt number, state the reasons for reversal, and include a legal memorandum demonstrating that the name is distinctive, not in conflict with pre-existing registrations, and free of prohibited tokens. The original reservation cannot be extended; upon favorable final decision, the name is restored only for the unexpired portion of the initial 30-day window. If the appeal is unsuccessful, a new reservation must be filed with a different proposed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the VPN and digital encryption software entity because no statutory physical business presence is required for a foreign-owned, non-licensed technology company. The registered office must be the office of a duly licensed resident agent in Panama, capable of receiving service of process. A mere unstaffed mailbox does not satisfy the statutory requirement. Payment processors and corporate banks may nevertheless impose their own requirement of a physical operating address before onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10-15% annually (low). The Registro Público does not conduct unannounced physical inspections of ordinary non-regulated companies. The UAF and the licensed resident agent may audit AML records; physical inspections of beneficial owners' premises occur only upon a money-laundering investigation, a judicial order, or a specific SAR-driven supervisory inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Panama Corporations Law), as amended, principally Arts. 5 (capital), 7-26 (formation and inscription), 53-59 (directors); Ley 5 de 2015 (Registered Agents) as amended; Código Fiscal (Fiscal Code) Arts. 971 et seq. for RUC and tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Entities Division).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (Public Deed) containing the Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation), executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow-account requirement under Law 32 of 1927. The Articles typically fix nominal capital of US$10,000 subscribed in 100 registered shares of US$100.00 par value each; proof of payment or deposit is not required at inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A.

With a quorum present, the Directors unanimously resolved:

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The initial capital of US$10,000.00, represented by 100 ordinary registered shares of US$100.00 each, is hereby subscribed by the founding shareholders.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is established in Panama City, Republic of Panama, at the Corporate Agent's office, [AGENT FIRM].

3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The following are elected: President — [NAME]; Secretary — [NAME]; Treasurer — [NAME], to serve until the next annual general meeting.

4. AUTHORIZATION: The President is authorized to execute tax, banking, and regulatory filings under Law 32 of 1927.

APPROVED on ______, 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Check and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas (online search and reservation through the Public Registry portal or a licensed registered agent).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked corporate names ending in 'S.A.' for an official availability search. Once a name is accepted, pay the reservation fee and hold the name for 30 days while the Public Deed is drafted.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copies of incorporators
Registered agent engagement letter
Name search request confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If all proposed names conflict with existing registrations, file new alternative names; rejected names carry no penalty and no cooling-off period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel drafts the Public Deed containing corporate name, commercial object (VPN, digital encryption networking, and network-security SaaS provision), renewable corporate term, capital structure, first board of directors, and appointment of the Registered Agent. The deed is read, approved, and executed by the incorporating shareholders before a Panamanian notary.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft Public Deed prepared by counsel
Passport copies of all incorporating shareholders
Written acceptance of the Registered Agent
Statement of subscribed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects, execute a release or correction within the same notarial protocol and re-execute the deed; no new reservation is required if the corporate name is unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registration Fees and Fiscal Stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (fiscal stamp counters) and Registro Público de Panamá collection office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the applicable stamp tax (papel sellado) and registry inscription tariff for a company with capital up to US$10,000; purchase the fiscal stamps, affix them to the Public Deed, and obtain an official payment receipt for submission with the deed.
required_dossiers: Executed Public Deed (unstamped draft)
Capital declaration of US$10,000
Statutory fee schedule and payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any deficiency in stamps is cured by purchasing supplementary fiscal stamps and re-submitting the deed with a consolidated payment receipt to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the stamped Public Deed and fee receipt for inscription. Standard review produces a certified inscription of the Sociedad Anónima within approximately 7 business days; an express 24-hour service is available at an additional statutory tariff for urgent closings.
required_dossiers: Original executed Public Deed bearing fiscal stamps
Official payment receipt
Application for certified incorporation certificate
Power of attorney or counsel engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry attaches observations (notas), counsel files a rectification brief within 30 business days; if the term lapses, the deed is archived and must be re-presented with updated documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Inscription Legalization: RUC, Corporate Books, and Municipal Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panamá; licensed public accountant for book legalization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certified certificate of inscription, register the company in the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC), legalize the corporate books (Share Ledger and Minutes Book) with the DGI, then file the Aviso de Operación at the Municipality of Panama together with the Fire Prevention Certificate and occupancy documentation for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Public Deed
Passport or ID of directors and President
Lease agreement for the Panamanian office
Corporate ledger books (share register and minutes book)
Cuerpo de Bomberos fire prevention certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: DGI queries are cured by resubmitting the certified deed and correcting the sworn declaration; municipal queries are cured by supplementing missing permits, lease certification, or locational documentation within the municipality's indicated term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral manufacturing or industrial license applies to VPN or network-security software SaaS activity; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) records commercial trade names and the Municipalidad de Panamá administers the business-operating permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Notice of Operation) for office-based software and technology services, issued by the Municipalidad de Panamá.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III — Exempt / no EIA study required (Executive Decree 123 of 2009, as amended by Executive Decree 11 of 2016); office-based software and data-processing services are not enumerated in the project annexes requiring EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge points. Office wastewater is discharged to municipal sanitary sewers under the Municipalidad de Panamá ordinance; no VOC or hazardous air-emission thresholds apply. E-waste and solid-waste segregation and disposal must comply with Ley 6 de 2018 (Basura Cero); any physical server hardware must be hosted by data-center operators maintaining ISO 14001 environmental management certification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá — mandatory inspection and annual Fire Prevention Certificate (Certificado de Prevención de Incendios) required to issue or renew the Aviso de Operación; Dirección de Ingeniería Municipal — occupancy certificate and structural load inspection of the registered office; MITRADEL — workplace health and safety compliance under Cabinet Decree No. 69 of 1970 (Reglamento de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial), including emergency evacuation plans and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online portal: Sede Electrónica (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa) and E-Tax 2.0 platform for corporate registrations, filings, and payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a resident agent and file a Notarized Public Deed or Certificate of Incorporation with the Public Registry. Subsequently, the agent submits Form RUC-101 to DGI to obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC), accompanied by the corporate charter, identity documents of directors, proof of registered address, and (if applicable) a Panama-source activity declaration. The RUC is issued within approximately 15 business days and is mandatory for ITBMS registration and customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope. A Panama Sociedad Anónima is taxed as a separate juridical person on Panama-source income only; foreign-source income is not taxable. Non-resident shareholders are permitted, and the entity is not automatically eligible for pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Panama does not allow optional pass-through for an S.A. However, taxpayers may elect for group consolidation under the special affiliated-company regime (Ley 66 de 2017 / Executive Decree 286 of 2017), subject to DGI approval. Hybrid mismatch elections may be available through the permanent-establishment rules of the Panama tax code and double-taxation treaties, but no unilateral elective branch-stripping mechanism is provided.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold; any person undertaking taxable transfers of movable goods or taxable services in Panama must obtain RUC and ITBMS registration. The simplified small-taxpayer regime may apply when gross annual income does not exceed USD 36,000 (B/.36,000 equivalent in Balboas, pegged to USD).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has a phased mandatory electronic invoicing regime (Factura Electrónica de Panamá). Taxpayers must issue invoices through DGI-approved software or the DGI web portal, transmitting real-time XML files to DGI for validation. Invoices must include a unique authorization code and QR code issued by DGI. There is no continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance engine equivalent to some Latin American jurisdictions, but offline systems require periodic transmission. Special provisions apply to simplified taxpayers. Failure to use compliant electronic invoicing may trigger exclusion from input VAT credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the sale or transfer of movable goods that leave Panamanian customs territory, as well as services rendered entirely abroad or effectively used outside Panama by non-residents, provided the exporter is a registered ITBMS taxpayer and holds the applicable export declaration. Digital VPN/privacy services may qualify as zero-rated offshore services when the recipient is a non-resident, the service is not connected with Panama-source economic activity, and the provider demonstrates territorial use abroad under DGI criteria.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración Aduanera de Exportación (electronic export declaration filed via the SICE customs platform)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (or digital service contract for offshore SaaS with non-resident client)
Service Agreement evidencing recipient's domicile outside Panama (for cross-border digital services)
Payment and inward remittance records (bank SWIFT or Settlement Statement showing foreign consideration)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may conduct a full audit with access to bank records, customs data, and e-invoice metadata. False zero-rating claims trigger retroactive ITBMS assessment at 7% plus surcharges (25% to 100% of the tax deficiency), interest accruing monthly, and fines for forged documentation. Criminal penalties may include imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for tax fraud, and the exporter loses the right to claim refunds or credits for up to two consecutive fiscal years. Directors and the resident agent may be jointly liable if fraudulent intent is proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no classical central bank. The U.S. dollar is full legal tender; the Balboa (PAB) exists only as a nominal coin parity unit. Banking supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decreto Ley 2 de 2008, monetary policy is effectively determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve, and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) coordinates fiscal and debt policy. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent to the State but has no monetary authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized, freely convertible jurisdiction with no exchange-control legislation. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted; there are no central bank approvals, no prior import/export licensing for currency flows, and no restrictions on profit remittance. Dividends paid by a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima out of taxed territorial income are subject to a 4% dividend withholding tax; dividends sourced from foreign-source income are exempt from withholding, subject to DGI formalities. The territorial income tax system therefore creates no treasury blockage for inbound capital or outbound distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no export invoice certification by any central bank. VPN subscription and SaaS export receipts may be retained 100% in U.S. dollars. Service revenue derived from non-Panamanian customers is treated as foreign-source income and is outside Panamanian territorial income tax, although the taxpayer must evidence the foreign situs of the service through customer contracts and payment-rail settlement records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium as payment-collection corridor, Low as primary liquidity-holding venue. Panama's fintech rule-making under Decreto Ley 218 de 2021 permits SBP-supervised financial innovation sandboxes, but no regulatory passport exists for a foreign Electronic Money Institution (EMI). An offshore EMI (e.g., an FCA or BaFin-regulated entity) may neither take deposits nor provide payment services to the Panamanian public without SBP authorization. For this VPN SaaS, Stripe and Paymentwall are acceptable as inbound collection routers and settlement agents, but treasury balances must be swept to a licensed SBP bank account in USD; the foreign EMI must not hold the company's operating reserve.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under SBP Rule 003-2021 and Law 23 of 2015, face-to-face verification is the default for a non-resident Medium-Risk Enhanced corporate client; remote onboarding is legally possible only with strengthened due diligence comprising apostilled and certified corporate documents, a registered-agent certificate, notarized board resolutions, and a live video interview. In practice, Tier-1 banks customarily require at least one beneficial owner or authorized signatory to appear physically at a Panamanian branch for final compliance interview, particularly because the SaaS scope (VPN/privacy application) elevates money-laundering risk. Towerbank and select private-banking desks will accept fully remote opening through a licensed third-party KYC intermediary, subject to SBP audit conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry classification as a privacy-enhancing VPN application: perceived anonymity that may facilitate undisclosed fund movements or circumvention of sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SaaS business plan; customer-acceptance and anti-abuse policy; merchant KYC/KYB records maintained for each subscription customer; proof that the company does not anonymize payment flows; Paymentwall and Stripe merchant agreements with settlement statistics; data-processing policy aligned with Law 81 of 2019 on personal data protection; sanctions-screening procedure documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the Panamanian S.A. ownership, in particular immobilized bearer shares, nominee shareholders, or incomplete UBO files.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Immobilization certificate for bearer shares under Law 23 of 2015; UBO registry extract filed with the Registro Público; resident-agent sworn statement identifying the final beneficial owner; certified share ledger and constitutive documents with Spanish-legalized translation; directors' resolution approving account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket cross-border subscription inflows without a demonstrable end-user base, a pattern typical of money mules or card-testing fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Paymentwall settlement reports geo-tagged by issuing country; chargeback and refund policy documentation; bank statements explaining payment-density; reviewed or audited financial statements of the S.A.; exemplar invoices and license agreements; application-server logs confirming genuine consumer traffic; sworn statement from the CFO on revenue composition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outflows to high-risk infrastructure counterparties such as foreign data centers, VPS resellers, crypto-exchanges, or unregulated gateway processors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cloud-hosting contracts with reputable providers (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud, Akamai); supplier due-diligence questionnaires; DGI tax-rating certificate (Solvencia Fiscal) proving good standing; monthly treasury plan matching invoices to settled subscription revenue; evidence of FX hedging or vendor payment policy excluding sanctioned payees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections enter via SWIFT MT103 to the U.S.-dollar account with an SBP-licensed bank. The wire must carry the shareholder legal name and the narrative 'Aporte de Capital — SOCIEDAD ANÓNIMA' in the sender-to-receiver information; the receiving bank registers the transaction as an equity contribution in its capital records. FX authorization is not required because Panama lacks exchange controls; however, any large credit (typically USD 50,000 or more, per bank policy) triggers source-of-funds verification. The account-opening KYC file should pre-certify the shareholder's wealth source to avoid suspension of inbound credits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recurring VPN infrastructure costs are settled by SWIFT MT103 corporate payments through the bank's dollar account, with correspondent clearing executed in New York (or Miami for LATAM corridors). Commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) are structurally unnecessary for SaaS and should be reserved for large hardware or sub-marine cable/bandwidth procurement where L/C terms are requested by the vendor. Domestic USD transactions of the Panamanian entity and local counterparties settle via the SBP-supervised electronic clearing (ACH Panama) and the local interbank network; same-day USD is available within the local clearing group. FX-related foreign-currency disbursements (EUR, GBP) are converted at the bank's treasury desk and cleared via the correspondent MT103, with no central bank approval or surrender obligation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (EUR/USD and GBP/USD, tenors up to 12 months) offered by SBP-licensed commercial banks and international counterparts
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for major pairs executed through SBP-authorized treasury desks
Vanilla FX Options (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) for hedging subscription-revenue volatility

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on LATAM currencies (e.g., COP, BRL, MXN) booked offshore or via local treasury pages, permissible because Panama maintains no functioning domestic money market in currencies other than the U.S. dollar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Único de Mantenimiento) and Registered Agent Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; coordinated through the licensed resident agent and referenced in the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before March 31, irrespective of the incorporation anniversary; the resident agent must receive funds sufficiently in advance to process payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory interest and a late-payment surcharge; the company is barred from obtaining the Paz y Salvo fiscal certificate and cannot complete share transfers or property recordals; two consecutive unpaid years may trigger administrative suspension and eventual strike-off by the Registro Público

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Share Register Confirmation (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá through the licensed resident agent; information remains non-public and is accessible only to authorized authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual franchise tax renewal before March 31; any shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change must additionally be declared within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update or confirm beneficial ownership records constitutes an administrative offense under Law 52 of 2016, subject to fines per unregistered record, and imposes a transactional block with the Registro Público until the record is rectified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de ISLR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, on or before March 31. Prepayments and monthly quota payments are made throughout the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues statutory fines and interest from the original due date; continued non-filing permits DGI administrative assessment and registration of tax liens against corporate assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit by a Panamanian Certified Public Accountant (Contador Público Autorizado) is mandatory when total annual gross revenues exceed USD 3,000,000, total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or when shareholders representing at least 10% of issued shares request a statutory audit. Regulated financial, insurance, and public-interest entities are audited irrespective of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; small and medium-sized entities may apply the IFRS for SMEs framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed resident agent acts as custodian of the beneficial ownership register. At the time of each annual franchise tax renewal, the agent must confirm the identity of all current shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners. Any share transfer, share issuance, or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the internal register and reflected in the custodian's records within 30 days of the event. Confirmation is made by a signed certificate or updated electronic filing with the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales, and the register is not available for public inspection unless required by court order or a competent supervisory authority.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Libro de Registro de Accionistas
Register of Directors / Libro de Registro de Directores
Register of Officers / Libro de Registro de Oficiales (Presidente, Secretario, Tesorero, Fiscal)
Minute Book for Shareholders' Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 – USD 2,500 per year depending on the resident agent and included compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 for a typical VPN/network-privacy SaaS company; higher for entities meeting the compulsory audit threshold with complex multi-entity operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific tax holiday for ISIC 6201 (VPN software); territorial system excludes foreign-source income; general deductions for operating expenses, depreciation of software and capital equipment, research and development staff costs; the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2017 may provide a reduced effective rate for certified headquarters entities, but this depends on the DGI and INDOCAL authorizations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 730 – Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta (Legal Entity Annex 731); filed electronically through the DGI Digital / E-Tax portal (https://www.dgi.gob.pa) using the taxpayer’s RUC and e-signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 31 March of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year authorized by the DGI, within three months of the fiscal year-end date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian Registro Único de Contribuyentes assigned to the Sociedad Anónima at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Panamanian RUC only; do not use the foreign shareholder’s identification number on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from VPN subscription fees, digital encryption licensing and network-security services where the services are used or economically sourced in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source income. Revenue from foreign server usage and subscription sales to non-resident users outside Panama is excluded under the territorial system; retain IP address and user-eligibility documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 – Cost of Sales and Operating Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct network costs, licensed software expenses, personnel salaries, depreciation, amortization of development costs and deductible operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be attributable to the production of taxable Panama-source revenue and supported by invoices in Panama; expenses incurred abroad are deductible only if they economically relate to Panama-source income and are properly documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Panamanian taxable income after deductions and application of net operating losses from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is a loss, carry it forward for a maximum of five fiscal years; a nil return must still be filed even if all income is foreign-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory corporate income tax applied to the taxable Panamanian-income base, reduced by advance payments and withholdings made during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax arises on exempt foreign-source income; keep a separate foreign-source income schedule in the working papers to support the exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the 10% dividend withholding tax on dividends distributed during the period, or 5% if the distribution originates from previously taxed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Panamanian S.A. must withhold and remit dividend WHT even when the distributing profits were generated abroad and the shareholder is non-resident; the director remains personally liable for unauthorised distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped at 50%, plus a minimum administrative fine of USD 100 when no tax is payable; late payment accrues statutory interest at 10% per annum; repeat non-filing can result in fines up to USD 5,000, suspension of the RUC, and a travel ban for the responsible director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on payments of dividends; reduced to 5% for dividends paid out of profits already subject to the 25% corporate rate; no withholding on distributions from accumulated foreign-source reserves that were never subject to Panamanian tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a double-tax-avoidance agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home-country tax authority; (ii) legalize or apostille the TRC and add a declaration of beneficial-ownership and absence of a Panamanian permanent establishment; (iii) deliver the package to the paying Panamanian corporation before the dividend record date; (iv) the corporation files the request and supporting dossier with the DGI via E-Tax; upon DGI approval the reduced DTA rate (usually 0%-10%) is applied; any excess WHT can be refunded within the five-year statute of limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical-assistance fees sourced in Panama carry a statutory withholding tax of 12.5%; DTA rates range from 0% to 10% (e.g., Mexico 10%, South Korea 10%, United Kingdom 0% under specified conditions). Interest on genuine foreign commercial loans is generally exempt from Panamanian withholding tax under the territorial system; however, interest on bearer instruments or excessive back-to-back loans may be recharacterized as dividends and taxed at 10% under thin-capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 5,000,000 in annual related-party transactions triggers a mandatory Local File; a Master File is required for a multinational group when the worldwide consolidated gross revenue exceeds USD 50,000,000. Under the thresholds, only a declaration annex in Form 730 is required, but the taxpayer must still apply the arm’s length principle.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has not enacted a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; nevertheless, the DGI and the Financial Intelligence Unit apply a substance-over-form analysis under the Código Fiscal. A VPN/privacy software S.A. must maintain a registered agent, a Panamanian statutory seat and board minutes; if treaty benefits or banking services are sought, the company must additionally show a qualified director, local payroll or administration, and real economic activity proportional to revenue. Inadequate substance can trigger denial of deductions, recharacterization of income by the shareholder's home jurisdiction, and cancellation of the RUC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally underreporting Panama-source VPN subscription or licensing revenue; inflating expenses via fake related-party invoices; using nominee shareholders to conceal the ultimate beneficiary or failing to remit dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty equal to 50% of the evaded tax plus statutory interest; deliberate evasion exceeding USD 100,000 triggers criminal prosecution under Law 38 of 2017 with imprisonment of 2 to 8 years and a fine of up to USD 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The DGI may disregard the S.A.'s limited-liability veil when the corporate form was used to evade tax; the director becomes jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties, faces a travel ban (pedimento de salida), and may be disqualified from managing companies in Panama for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A. as a pure shell with nominee directors and no real VPN service activity; refusing or incorrectly filing the mandatory Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) declaration with the Panamanian registry under Law 254 of 2021; accepting untraceable crypto subscriptions without internal business control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty of USD 5,000 to USD 25,000 imposed on the company; UBO non-compliance accrues a recurring fine of USD 500 per month; the DGI can classify the entity as economically inactive, suspend the RUC, and cancel the registered agent's license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered agents who fail to ensure UBO disclosure are personally liable for statutory fines; Panamanian courts will pierce the veil and order civil restitution where the shell was used for fraudulent digital invoicing, trademark infringement, or money laundering; exit bans and personal asset embargos apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering via Anonymous VPN Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Enabling anonymous use of the VPN platform for payment-card laundering, ransomware extortion proceeds, or narcotics-money movement; admitting transactions from sanctioned wallets or facilitating
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 254 of 2021, fines range from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 and the company may lose operational authorizations; criminal money laundering of criminal proceeds carries 5 to 12 years of imprisonment and a fine of up to 300% of the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly or with willful blindness fail to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) are criminally liable; upon conviction, the S.A. veil is pierced, allowing personal confiscation of assets, extradition waivers, travel bans and imprisonment in Panamanian adult correctional facilities.
